video_title: Full Denver Nuggets Postgame Media Availability vs. BOS 🎙

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on the challenge of managing the second unit rotation
quotes.excerpt: I have to find a way for that second five can hold water and Demar did it.
quotes.quote: We have changed our rotation a lot. A lot of teams do that. Boston plays Tatum in the first and the third. I felt like if we play them through the 12, we get Demar in there. You kind of play the front end of your roster and you try to play athletic and different to start the second. Some of it was good, some of it was bad. I have to find a way for that second five can hold water and Demar did it in the fourth quarter. It has to complement everybody. It cannot just be how does the second unit work, it is what is best for Jamal and Nicola too, and Aaron.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman on the Nuggets second unit rotation: I have to find a way for that second five can hold water. It cannot just be how does the second unit work, it is what is best for Jamal and Nicola too, and Aaron.

structured.context: Coach Adelman discusses his rotation strategy against Boston and how he manages minutes for his key players.

quotes.speaker: Coach Adelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Coach Adelman on Aaron's aggressive play and finding his rhythm
quotes.excerpt: I think he should be aggressive. I know he turned the ball over a few times.
quotes.quote: I think he should be aggressive. I know he turned the ball over a few times, but also put your head on the rim constantly. I think the best way to find a rhythm is if you have what he has, size and the ability to get to the free throw line. This league has told us that forever. Guys struggle to shoot the ball. If you can find the free throw line, it really can restart you. And that has been a thing in our league forever. And to have the ability to get to the line like he does, I think for all our guys, that is a restart in a real game.
quotes.social_post: Coach Adelman on Aaron: I think the best way to find a rhythm is if you have what he has, size and the ability to get to the free throw line. That is a restart in a real game.

structured.context: Coach Adelman explains why he encourages Aaron Gordon to remain aggressive and seek out free throws to find his rhythm.

quotes.speaker: Demar Derozan
quotes.summary_phrase: Demar Derozan on the learning curve of coming off the bench
quotes.excerpt: I would be lying to you to tell you it ain't tough. It is tough.
quotes.quote: I would be lying to you to tell you it ain't tough. It is tough. We are 12, 13 games in, still so much learning, trying to get comfortable with it, get accustomed to doing something for the first time in 17 years. So, just try to figure out how, when, how much I can dictate the game when I am out there, what I see before I go in there. Every moment has been a learning curve for me. Just want to continue to get better at it.
quotes.social_post: Demar Derozan on coming off the bench: I would be lying to you to tell you it ain't tough. It is tough. I am trying to get accustomed to doing something for the first time in 17 years.

structured.context: Demar Derozan reflects on the difficulty of adjusting to a bench role after seventeen years as a starter.

quotes.speaker: Jamal Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Murray on the importance of controlling the game's tempo
quotes.excerpt: We can control the tempo, I think, and the pace of the game.
quotes.quote: We can control the tempo, I think, and the pace of the game. I think that is another big thing. It is not just about possessions and efficiency, it is also about the tempo. Phoenix, they were moving the ball and a lot of their actions were at the top of the key and they were swinging it and they were getting downhill off these passes. Obviously, we are getting tired after they grab a rebound and doing it over and over again. So, I think stuff like that has a play in it. We can decide if we want to run, we can decide if we want to stop or slow down.
quotes.social_post: Jamal Murray on controlling the pace: We can decide if we want to run, we can decide if we want to stop or slow down. It is not just about possessions and efficiency, it is also about the tempo.

structured.context: Jamal Murray discusses the importance of controlling game tempo and pace, referencing recent observations from a game against Phoenix.

quotes.speaker: Jamal Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Murray on the challenge of balancing offense and defense
quotes.excerpt: Just play hard on both ends and if you need a sub, call for it.
quotes.quote: Just play hard on both ends and if you need a sub, call for it. That is my philosophy right now, just play hard and there is no babying in one side of the court. If I am on the court, I am playing as hard as I can. It just so happens that I am staying in front of guys a little better and getting deflections and we are going the other way. But in terms of effort and energy, it is always constant. I tell the DA, if I need a sub, I will let you know.
quotes.social_post: Jamal Murray on his current philosophy: Just play hard on both ends and if you need a sub, call for it. There is no babying in one side of the court. If I am on the court, I am playing as hard as I can.

structured.context: Jamal Murray explains his current approach to balancing high-intensity play on both ends of the court.

quotes.speaker: Jamal Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Murray on different ways to win games
quotes.excerpt: Every game is different, it calls for different types of things, different personnel and different strengths.
quotes.quote: Every game is different, it calls for different types of things, different personnel and different strengths and weaknesses. But I think, our defense and intensity, every time I notice that we are playing super aggressive intense defense, I feel like it always works well for us. Whether they score or whatever happens, I feel like it always, we pick up our energy on offense. We have more of a will to win, we get the crowd fired up and stuff like that. The biggest thing is just energy and effort, constantly through 48.
quotes.social_post: Jamal Murray on team intensity: Every time I notice that we are playing super aggressive intense defense, I feel like it always works well for us. We pick up our energy on offense.

structured.context: Jamal Murray highlights how defensive intensity and energy consistently fuel the team's offensive performance.

quotes.speaker: Jamal Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamal Murray on the process of building team identity
quotes.excerpt: I don't think there is a really good answer to that, honestly. It just takes time.
quotes.quote: I don't think there is a really good answer to that, honestly. It just takes time. There is a lot of different factors that go into it and different teams play different defenses and it calls for different lineups and stuff like that. But I think we are starting to figure out where the offense can come from and the speed that we can play with different units and what each unit needs to figure out what can help them win the game, whether it is rebounding together and taking possession by possession or if it is grab and go. I think there is a lot of different ways that we can impact the game with different lineups. Still figuring it out, it is not going to be perfect, but we are building in the right direction each game.
quotes.social_post: Jamal Murray on building team identity: I don't think there is a really good answer to that, honestly. It just takes time. We are starting to figure out where the offense can come from.

structured.context: Jamal Murray discusses the ongoing process of building team identity and finding effective lineup combinations.
